senses.gloss: A large lamp at the front of a car or truck that lights the road ahead.
examples: A rock cracked the driver's-side *headlamp*.
The truck's *headlamps* cut through the fog.
Replacing a burned-out *headlamp* took me ten minutes.

senses.gloss: The single most important point of a report, a speech, or a set of results.
examples: The *headline* from the earnings call was a 20 percent jump in sales.
Skip the details for now and just give me the *headline*.
The *headline* of the study is that the drug works better in older patients.

senses.gloss: The cloth-covered lining on the inside of a car's roof.
examples: The *headliner* in my old Civic is starting to sag.
A leak around the sunroof stained the *headliner*.
The shop quoted me three hundred dollars to replace the *headliner*.

senses.gloss: A shot or blow that hits someone in the head, especially in a video game.
examples: He won the round with a single *headshot*.
In this game a *headshot* counts double.
She landed three *headshots* in a row and the other team quit.

senses.gloss: A force or condition that slows something down, especially in business or the economy.
examples: The company is facing serious *headwinds* going into next year.
Higher interest rates are a *headwind* for the housing market.
Sales grew anyway, despite all the *headwinds*.

senses.gloss: A very short moment of time.
examples: I'd take that job in a *heartbeat*.
Everything changed in a *heartbeat*.
She would move back to Chicago in a *heartbeat* if they asked.

senses.gloss: One of the two halves of the brain.
examples: Language is handled mostly by the left *hemisphere*.
The stroke damaged the right *hemisphere*.
The two *hemispheres* are joined by a thick band of nerve fibers.

senses.gloss: The group of people who hold the top positions in an organization.
examples: The church *hierarchy* refused to comment on the report.
Nobody in the company's *hierarchy* would take responsibility.
The decision came straight from the party *hierarchy*.

senses.gloss: The lightest, brightest area of a photograph or a painting.
examples: The photo is overexposed and the *highlights* are completely blown out.
Pull the *highlights* down a little and the sky will come back.
A single white *highlight* in each eye makes the portrait look alive.

senses.gloss: A cosmetic that puts a shine on the cheekbones and other high points of the face.
examples: She dusted a little *highlighter* along her cheekbones.
This *highlighter* gives a soft glow instead of glitter.
I keep my *highlighter* and my blush in the same drawer.

senses.gloss: The best moments of a game or event, especially shown afterward as a short video.
examples: I missed the game, so I watched the *highlights* on my phone.
The station shows *highlights* from every Sunday game.
The team posted the *highlights* right after the final whistle.

senses.gloss: A person's return home after being away for a long time.
examples: The whole family drove to the airport for his *homecoming*.
After two years overseas, her *homecoming* felt strange.
The town threw a party to celebrate the soldiers' *homecoming*.

senses.gloss: A short early period in which a new leader or arrangement is treated kindly before the criticism starts.
examples: The mayor's *honeymoon* with the press lasted about a month.
Every new manager gets a *honeymoon*, and then the complaints begin.
The *honeymoon* is over — the board wants results this quarter.

senses.gloss: The business of running hotels, restaurants, and other places that serve guests.
senses.ru: гостиничный и ресторанный бизнес, индустрия гостеприимства
examples: She has worked in *hospitality* since she was nineteen.
The college offers a two-year degree in *hospitality*.
*Hospitality* was the hardest-hit industry during the shutdown.

senses.gloss: Fighting in a war, used in the plural.
examples: *Hostilities* broke out along the border in the spring.
Both sides agreed to a pause in *hostilities* over the holiday.
The treaty formally ended *hostilities* after four years.

senses.gloss: The removal of a number of people from an organization in order to fix it.
examples: The new owner did some *housecleaning* in the front office.
After a losing season, fans expected a major *housecleaning*.
The scandal led to a *housecleaning* at the top of the agency.

senses.gloss: Small routine matters that have to be dealt with before the real business begins.
examples: A little *housekeeping* before we start: the restrooms are down the hall.
The first ten minutes of the meeting were pure *housekeeping*.
We got the *housekeeping* out of the way and moved on to the budget.

senses.gloss: The academic subjects that study human culture, such as literature, history, and philosophy, used in the plural.
examples: She majored in the *humanities* and then went to law school.
Federal funding for the *humanities* has been cut again.
The college requires two years of *humanities* before you can graduate.

senses.gloss: A ship built to break through sea ice and open a path for other vessels.
examples: An *icebreaker* cleared a channel to the port.
The research team sailed north aboard a nuclear *icebreaker*.
Two *icebreakers* work the Great Lakes all winter.

senses.gloss: The act of recognizing or naming what something is or who someone is.
examples: *Identification* of the body took several days.
Early *identification* of the disease saves lives.
The lab handles *identification* of unknown samples.

senses.gloss: The act of catching fire, or the moment something starts to burn.
examples: A spark caused the *ignition* of gas that had built up in the basement.
The fire investigator was looking for the point of *ignition*.
The countdown reached zero and we had *ignition*.

senses.gloss: The act of copying the way someone else behaves, speaks, or works.
examples: Children learn most of what they know by *imitation*.
His early paintings were pure *imitation* of his teacher.
*Imitation* is the sincerest form of flattery.

senses.gloss: A performance in which someone copies another person's voice and manner, usually to be funny.
examples: He does a great *imitation* of his history teacher.
Her *imitation* of the boss had everyone in tears.
He ran through his *imitations* of all the neighbors.
